must_remember: Optically active substances lack a center and plane of symmetry, possessing molecular or crystalline asymmetry.
Circular birefringence refers to the phenomenon where a medium exhibits different refractive indices for left-circular ($n_L$) and right-circular ($n_R$) polarized light.
Biot's law states that the angle of rotation is directly proportional to path length ($l$) and concentration ($c$), and inversely proportional to the square of the wavelength ($\lambda^2$).
Specific rotation is defined at a path length of $1$ decimetre ($10\text{ cm}$) and concentration of $1\text{ g/cm}^3$ at a specified temperature and wavelength.
Linearly polarized light is equivalent to two oppositely rotating circular vibrations of equal amplitude and frequency.
Specific rotation is an intensive property and is independent of the length of the polarimeter tube or concentration used.

glossary.meaning: The ability of a substance to rotate the plane of polarization of linearly polarized light passing through it.
The property of an optically active medium where left-circular and right-circular polarized components travel with different phase velocities ($v_L \neq v_R$).
Rotation produced by a solution of length $1\text{ dm}$ and concentration $1\text{ g/cm}^3$ under specified conditions.
Relates optical rotation angle $\theta$ to path length $l$, concentration $c$, and wavelength $\lambda$.
Geometrical property of a rigid object (or molecule) of being non-superimposable on its mirror image, lacking reflection symmetry.

comparisons.title: Extensive vs Intensive Property
rows: Extensive property (depends on path length and concentration)
Intensive property (characteristic constant of the substance)
